# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 54 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 54 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_054_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 5, Introduction — The Fasting Parable

**54:1** As I was fasting and sitting on a certain mountain and giving thanks to the Lord for all that he had done for me, I saw the Shepherd sitting down beside me and saying: "Why have you come here so early?" "Because, lord," I said, "I have a duty of observance." "What is this duty of observance?" he asked. "I am keeping a fast, lord," I said. "What is this fast," he said, "that you are observing?"

**54:2** "As I have been accustomed, lord," I said. "You do not know," he said, "how to fast to the Lord. This useless fast that you are observing before him is not a fast." "Why then, lord?" I said. "I tell you," he said, "that this fast is not a fast, which you suppose to be a fast. But I will teach you what a fast is that is complete and acceptable to the Lord.

**54:3** Listen," he said. "God does not desire such a vain fast. For by fasting to God in this way, you accomplish nothing for righteousness. But offer to God a fast of this kind: do no evil in your life, and serve the Lord with a pure heart; keep his commandments, walking in his ordinances, and let no evil desire arise in your heart. Trust God. If you do these things, and fear him and abstain from every evil deed, you shall live to God; and if you do these things, you shall accomplish a great fast and one acceptable to God."

---

*EMET renders the Greek of P.Mich. 130 with maximal literalness, preserving the redefinition of fasting at the opening of Similitude 5.*
